newsitem.title: USA: EMC to unveil upgrades to storage systems.
newsitem.headline: EMC to unveil upgrades to storage systems.

text.p: EMC Corp will unveil Tuesday a major upgrade of its Symmetrix storage systems for servers and mainframe computer systems, a move analysts said is necessary for EMC to stay ahead of its encroaching rivals.

The Hopkington, Mass.-based storage company said in an advisory that it is holding a press conference on Tuesday in Manhattan to make an "important technology announcement." But no other details were available from EMC.
Analysts said EMC is unveiling across-the-board upgrades of its disk systems with major performance improvements.

"EMC has turbocharged their subsystem," said Thomas Lahive, an analyst at International Data Corp. "The net result will be you have a higher capacity, higher performance product at a lower cost for the user."

Analysts said EMC's upgrade includes new models in its 3000 Series of subsystems for open systems and its 5000 Series of subsystems for mainframe computers. The new subsystems will increase storage space with the latest in high-density drives.
EMC needs to upgrade its disk drive systems because of recent and soon-to-be announced product offerings from its disk drive competitors and some non disk drive competitors.

"It's very important for EMC to do this," said Thomas Lahive, an analyst at International Data Corp in Framingham, Mass. "It's an upgrade ...but it was essential that they do a performance upgrade. Many vendors have been claiming that EMC doesn't do this this and this."

Analysts said some vendors have either announced their own new storage products or have plans to. International Business Machines Corp, through its alliance with Storage Technology Corp, will unveil some storage upgrades in February. And next week, Sun Microsystems Inc is expected to announce mainframe-like capacity storage systems.
"They have to do this stuff to stay competitve with what StorageTek and therefore IBM, Hitachi and others are doing," said Gary Helmig, a SoundView Financial Group analyst.

According to Computerworld, a trade magazine, EMC will unveil three new models of storage disk arrays for the open systems/server market, the Symmetrix 3330, 3430 and 3700, priced at $625,000, $1.5 million and $3.2 million, respectively.
For the mainframe market, Computerworld reported that EMC will launch the Symmetrix 5330, 5430 and 5700, priced at $682,000, $1.6 million and $3.4 million, respectively.
